transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
Well, it's a burning sensation when I pass water, and I'm needing to go ever so much more often than usual. It's been bothering me for a little while now.
Could you tell me how much this is affecting your day-to-day life, and whether you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?

It's been uncomfortable enough that I've stopped going to the residents' coffee morning, in case I can't reach a toilet in time. As for medicines, I'm allergic to trimethoprim — it gave me a dreadful itchy rash.
Could you tell me about any medicines you take regularly or have started or changed recently — and any health problems, operations, or hospital stays you’ve had in the past?

I take levothyroxine 75 micrograms every morning for my underactive thyroid, and alendronic acid 70 mg once a week for thin bones. I also use a vaginal cream from the hospital twice a week, but I can't remember what it's called. As for the past, I had a water infection about a year ago that was treated with antibiotics.
Other than the burning when you pass water and needing to go more often, have you noticed anything else that started around the same time or seems connected?

The urine looks cloudy and smells stronger than usual, though I haven't seen any blood. I've not had a fever, shivers, back or side pain, or vomiting, and my niece hasn't noticed any new confusion in me.
Can you tell me exactly where you feel the burning when you pass water, and whether it spreads anywhere?
It's just down below, when the water passes — a stinging feeling there. It doesn't spread anywhere else as far as I've noticed.

Besides the levothyroxine, alendronic acid, and the vaginal cream, is there anything else you take — for example, any other medicines for your thyroid or bones, or anything you were given for the water infection last year?
No, that's the lot — just those three. I don't take anything else for my thyroid or bones, and I wasn't given anything ongoing after the water infection last year.

Can you tell me how the burning and needing to go more often have been over time — for example, whether they come and go or stay about the same — and whether anything you’ve noticed seems to make them better or worse?
Oh, it's been about two weeks now. It's stayed much the same really — the stinging is about 5 out of 10, and I've not noticed anything that makes it better or worse.

You’ve mentioned the underactive thyroid, thin bones, and the water infection last year — is there anything else you see a doctor or nurse about regularly, any other health condition your medicines are for (including what the vaginal cream from the hospital is for), or any operations or hospital stays, or is that everything?

I don't see anyone else regularly, and I can't remember the name of the hospital cream or exactly what it's for, only that I use it twice a week. Apart from that, I've not had any operations or hospital stays — that's everything.
What worries you most about the burning and needing to go more often, and what are you hoping we can help with at your visit?
I think it's another water infection, like the one I had last year, and I'm hoping I can get some antibiotics before the weekend. That's what worries me most — being stuck like this over the weekend.
Since this started, have you noticed any changes in your appetite, sleep, weight or energy, or any changes in your bladder or bowel habits or breathing — or have those stayed the same?
My sleep's been broken because I'm up three or four times in the night, when usually it's just once. Otherwise I've not noticed any change in appetite, weight, energy, my bowels, or my breathing.
Is there anything else you’ve noticed since the burning and needing to go more often started that we haven’t talked about yet?
No, I don't think there's anything else — that's about the sum of it.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
